[Derive symmetric equilibrium for a 3-player third-price sealed-bid auction with uniform values: b(v)=2v. Intuition: when everyone uses an increasing bidding function, the best-response condition implies ∫_0^v b(t) dt = v^2, so b(v)=2v. With my value $34, the equilibrium bid is 2*34 = $68. Bidding $68 maximizes expected long-run profit if others use the same strategy.]

[This is a third-price (lowest) sealed-bid with 3 bidders. If others bid their values, bidding above the maximum possible opponent value ensures I win and pay the expected minimum of opponents (49/3), giving positive expected profit: 33 - 49/3 ≈ 16.67. To secure win without extreme overbidding, I’ll bid just above the maximum possible value (49), e.g., 49.1.]
